$comment: Template for the redaction rule set consumed by scripts/verify-public-tree.ts.
Copy this file to internal/redaction-rules.json and fill in the real values.
internal/ is gitignored, so the real rule set never enters the repository.
Never commit a populated copy of this file.
rules[].pattern is a JavaScript regular expression source string.
rules[].flags defaults to "i".
rules[].testValue is a confidential proof value that must match pattern.
It is mandatory under --require-rules and prevents impossible rules from
satisfying the release gate. Never use a production credential as a test value.
Writing patterns: leave literals unanchored here. These rules only
*detect*, so a substring match is the conservative choice -- it also
catches a name embedded in a longer identifier or hostname.
The opposite is true when you *substitute* a literal while scrubbing a
tree for release: there, anchor with \b on both sides. An unanchored
four-letter name also matches inside ordinary English words, so the
replacement lands mid-word and glues the placeholder into them. The
result reveals precisely which literal was replaced, which is worse than
no redaction at all. The structural "redaction damage" rule in
scripts/verify-public-tree.ts catches that mistake; fix the words rather
than silencing it with an allowlist entry.
forbiddenFileNames matches base file names case-insensitively.
allowlist maps a repository-relative path to the rule labels tolerated in it.
Synthetic credential fixtures are already covered by structuralAllowlist in
scripts/verify-public-tree.ts, so allowlist is usually empty here.
